This includes custom application packages as well as ros2_control packages compiled from source." and "Compiler warning from rclcpp::experimental::IntraProcessManager::do_intra_process_publish" with the log in the linked gist (https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2461). A second user confirmed it and supplied the fix PR #2492 ("this commit will fix the warning [-Wstringop-overflow=] #2461").

units_identified: any rclcpp client package that calls Publisher::publish() (e.g. ros2_controllers)
E2.evidence: The warning is raised by GCC 13 on rclcpp's own header template code (intra_process_manager.hpp:256, copy-constructing a std::vector<uint64_t> from sub_ids.take_shared_subscriptions) when it is instantiated in any client that calls publish(). The report says it appears for any such application ("Compile application that uses rclcpp::Publisher and calls publish()"), so it does not depend on any assumption between rclcpp and a particular client: it would occur with any correct peer. The fix (PR #2492) only rewrites that internal line to use the iterator-range constructor; no declared interface (API symbol, message, parameter) of rclcpp changed.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated: E2 stops at step 2 (internal). The trigger was a toolchain upgrade ("after upgrading rolling to Ubuntu 24.04"; the maintainer notes the binaries moved to Ubuntu 24.04), not a provider/consumer revision change.

E4.evidence: Not evaluated: E2 fails. (The effect is a compile-time warning, shown in the gist.)

ineligible_reason: E2 step 2 (internal): a compiler warning from GCC 13 on rclcpp's own header implementation of IntraProcessManager::do_intra_process_publish, triggered by any client that calls publish(); the fix is an internal one-line rewrite with no interface change.
notes: The gist shows two GCC 13 diagnostics inlined from rclcpp/experimental/intra_process_manager.hpp:256: '-Warray-bounds=' ("forming offset 8 is out of the bounds [0, 8]") and '-Wstringop-overflow=' ("writing between 9 and 9223372036854775807 bytes into a region of size 8 overflows the destination"). Fix: rclcpp PR #2492 'fix: init concatenated_vector with begin() & end()', merged into rolling 2024-04-08 as 63c2e2ef6f7367b4420e4fd0eab5d78b551cb794; the bartalor/rclcpp commit c5af35ce is the same change carried in a fork (same message, parent 117343dc). An alternative reading treats the two units as rclcpp and the GCC 13 toolchain shipped with Ubuntu 24.04; there is still no declared interface between them that changed, and a compiler is not a robotics unit in the sense of the tree, so the case stays internal. One commenter reports the warning broke his build because warnings are treated as errors in his project; that is a consequence of his build flags, not a separate interface failure.
